correctness.rationale: The normalized monomial matrix is derived exactly from the beta integral. Uniform Gamma-ratio and cell-variation bounds give a delta-independent Hilbert-Schmidt difference from a Mellin-convolution integral kernel. All positive integral trace moments follow by an explicitly integrable connected convolution cycle and rescaled anchoring; telescoping transfers them across the Hilbert-Schmidt difference. Compact-support moment determinacy yields the weighted spectral measure, fixed-threshold counting, and all fixed p>=2 Schatten coefficients. The Fourier transform is the standard beta integral. Independent numerical finite checks are supplementary, not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: A natural operator family has a sharp compactness threshold but previously lacked a quantitative description of what becomes noncompact. The result supplies an entire nontrivial singular-value counting profile, a finite limiting spectral measure and sharp blow-up coefficients simultaneously for all real Schatten exponents p>=2. The Mellin multiplier and logarithmic spatial mixing explain the transition; the p=2 and p=4 exact benchmarks are useful checkable special cases rather than the sole contribution.
